correctness.rationale: For all m>=3, c>0, B>0 and real p>=0, trace of a strictly convex scalar spectral function of the positive compressed Laplacian is strictly convex on the connected conductance domain. Individual edge weights inject into L; symmetry therefore forces the unique global optimizer to use a common weight on matching edges and another on nonmatching edges. The three Laplacian eigenvalue classes are 2(a+(m-1)b), mb (multiplicity m-1), 2a+(m-2)b (multiplicity m-1). Differentiation along the exact budget gives the claimed one-sided threshold c_m,p and unique interior scalar root. An explicit positive formula proves strict order monotonicity. The rescaled threshold yields the logistic crossover and shows noncommuting limits. The stationary derivative expansion proves the fixed-order critical-price conductance ratio. The standalone verifier passed 852 direct-eigenvalue, exact-rational, optimization and asymptotic diagnostics. These checks are supplementary to the analytic proof. Disconnected allocations are excluded explicitly.

originality.rationale: The checked primary scientific articles establish resistance design and first-/second-order coherence measures, not all-real-order matching-price support on the designated balanced biclique. Relevant published mathematical results separately give the determinant, first-order inverse trace and spectral-gap endpoints on exactly the same priced matching, so these endpoints are not claimed new. The new statement gives one exact frontier for every real p>=0, proves its strict dependence on p, and finds the previously unaccounted-for joint logistic scaling p/m -> alpha. Distinct finite-order and joint-order implications are not deducible from the three isolated endpoint values alone. A search is not proof of global novelty; the uninspected full text of public mathematical records and unindexed work remain specific publication risks.
residual_risks: Some directly relevant public mathematical record full texts were not accessible; their titles and summaries alone cannot establish whole-document noncoverage. A broader general spectral-moment interpolation theorem could be present in unavailable material.
Negative searches are not proof of worldwide priority; unindexed work or equivalent notation could cover the continuum of orders.
The claim is limited to exactly priced perfect-matching orbits on balanced complete bipartite graphs. It does not extend to heterogeneous edge pricing or all graph classes.

value.rationale: The mathematical question is the natural design decision to purchase or delete a redundant perfect matching when each edge carries a cost, under determinant, coherence and spectral criteria. The new theorem is not an isolated low-order calculation: it gives the complete continuous p>=0 hierarchy, its globally strict nesting, and a genuinely different joint order-network-size scaling law 2/(1+e^{-2alpha}), exhibiting noncommutation of limits 1 versus 2. Existing endpoint support theorems do not determine intermediate costs or this crossover. This supports future spectral-risk design choices. No constant-factor objective improvement or new general algorithm is claimed.
